newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - March 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - March 13.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English chemist Doctor JOSEPH PRIESTLEY, who discovered oxygen in 1774, was born on this day in 1733.
Legendary Englishman DANIEL LAMBERT, known for his weight of 335 kilograms (52 stone, 11 pounds), was born on this day in 1770. At 180 centimetres (5 feet, 11 inches), he was a 'big' man.
Queensland politician JOSHUA 'JOEY' BELL was born in 1863.
Australian inventor LANCELOT DE MOLE, who designed the tracked army tank in 1911 (but the War Office rejected the need for it), was born in 1880.
English novelist SIR HUGH WALPOLE ("The Herries Chronicle"), was born in 1884.
Tasmanian nurse CLARE DEACON, among the first nurses to win the Military Medal in the First World War in recognition of bravery, was born in 1891.
Australian physician and health writer LADY PHYLLIS CILENTO was born in 1894.
English entertainer TESSIE O'SHEA, known as "Two Ton Tessie" because of her size, was born in 1918.

American singer/songwriter NEIL SEDAKA was born in 1939. His first hit was "Oh Carol"(1959), which he dedicated to CAROLE KING. His biggest early hit was "Breaking Up Is Hard To Do" (1962). Hits in the seventies included "Laughter In The Rain" (1974) and "Bad Blood" (1975). He had a hit with his daughter DARA with "Should've Never Let You Go" (1980).
Hungarian-born heavyweight boxer 'Aussie' JOE BUGNER was born in 1950.
Irish bass player with 'U2' ADAM CLAYTON was born in 1960.
** EVENTS **
1781 : German astronomer WILLIAM HERSCHEL discovered
URANUS, but initially called the planet GEORGIUM SIDUS after his patron, England's GEORGE III. After much controversy, URANUS was selected, in keeping with the old mythological system of names.
1881 : Russian Tsar ALEXANDER II was murdered by
extremists, on the same day that he agreed to implement democratic reforms. Two bombs were thrown at him while he stood in a street in Saint Petersburg, the first missed but the second killed him.
1886 : British soldiers of all regiments and ranks were
first allowed to wear beards.
1894 : The first professional strip-tease was staged at
the Davan Fayoneau Music Hall in Paris.
1906 : American feminist SUSAN B. ANTHONY died.
1928 : 450 people drowned when the St. Francis dam burst
40 miles north of Los Angeles.
1930 : PLUTO was discovered by CLYDE TOMBAUGH, as a
result of calculations made by astronomer PERCIVAL LOWELL 14 years earlier.
1935 : A three-thousand-year-old archive was found in
Jersualem that reportedly supported parts of the Bible.
1961 : 79 year-old artist PABLO PICASSO married his 37
year-old model JACQUELINE ROCQUE.
1969 : Brisbane became the first Australian capital to
receive natural gas with the opening of the pipeline from Roma.
1972 : CLIFFORD IRVING admitted in a New York court to
having fabricated the 'autobiography' of HOWARD HUGHES.
1972 : Britain and China resumed full diplomatic
relations after 22 years; Britain withdrew its consulate from Taiwan.
1987 : Sydney's Supreme Court ruled that the memoirs of a

retired M15 officer PETER WRIGHT could be published. The British Government said it would appeal against the decision. They claim the book "Spycatcher" would endanger its national security and would open the way for other officers to release confidential information. In his book Mr WRIGHT claimed a former M15 head Sir ROGER HOLLIS was a Soviet spy.
1992 : Close to 600 people were killed when a massive
earthquake struck Turkey.
1994 : Former West Australian Premier CARMEN LAWRENCE won
a House of Representatives seat with an easy victory in the Fremantle by-election. Soon after she was given the health portfolio.
1995 : ODETTE HALLOWES, one of Britain's war heroines,
died. She became the first woman to be awarded the George Cross for gallantry for her work in occupied France in World War Two.
1996 : A man with four guns shot dead 16 children and a
woman teacher in a "slaughter of the innocents" at a school in Dunblane, Scotland. He then turned a gun on himself.
